description:
Sean Daly, chef/owner of Hugo in Oakley, has been invited to do a dinner at the  James Beard House in New York City. He’ll be packing up a refrigerated truck with pre-prepped items for a multi-course dinner and taking his kitchen crew to New York for the March 14 date.

The James Beard house is the former townhouse of James Beard, a cookbook writer  known for his championing  of classic American cuisine, his embrace of the good life, and influence on many American chefs. The James Beard Foundation invites chefs from all over the country to cook and serve a meal there throughout the year.  It’s generally considered a high honor. Daly’s excited. What to cook?  “Signature Hugo dishes for sure, then a compilation of things from over the years that I’ve done,” he said.  I’m guessing shrimp and grits will  be on the menu he’ll be working up soon.

Stan Kenton Alum John Von Ohlen kicks this band like no one else that iI can only describe as follows: ITS ALIVE! Don't try to analyze it, just feel it. Cammy award winner Steve Schmidt on piano and bassist MIke Sharfe drive this 17 piece band as well as anyone anywhere.

A legendary regional ensemble from Cincinnati, the Blue Wisp Big Band has, for the last thirty years, performed every Wednesday evening at the famed Blue Wisp Jazz Club in Cincinnati, owned and operated by Marjean Wisby until her passing in August 2006.

Having been around for a quarter of a century this big band knows how to play and does so with the same fire that has led them to record five acclaimed albums over the years. The musicians are seasoned pros with twelve of the sixteen players being original members.

The music is lively and buoyant, including a slew of sturdy solos from various players. Members include pianist Steve Schmidt, trumpeter Hank Mautner, alto saxophonists Jim Sherrick and Mike Andres, baritone saxophonist Larry Dickson, tenor saxophonists Joe Gaudio and Herbie Aronoff, trombonists Paul Piller and Clarence Pond, bassist Michael Sharfe and drummer John Von Ohlen.

This is the kind of big band music that aficionados of the genre can appreciate and love to hear often which is why the Blue Wisp Big Band is still around and producing some of the finest orchestrations you'll hear anywhere.

Containing world-class horn players and bolstered by a superlative rhythm section, this group has established a reputation that extends far beyond Cincinnati and will hopefully keep them playing for years to come.

description:
Stan Kenton Alum John Von Ohlen kicks this band like no one else that iI can only describe as follows: ITS ALIVE! Don't try to analyze it, just feel it. Cammy award winner Steve Schmidt on piano and bassist MIke Sharfe drive this 17 piece band as well as anyone anywhere.

A legendary regional ensemble from Cincinnati, the Blue Wisp Big Band has, for the last thirty years, performed every Wednesday evening at the famed Blue Wisp Jazz Club in Cincinnati, owned and operated by Marjean Wisby until her passing in August 2006.

Having been around for a quarter of a century this big band knows how to play and does so with the same fire that has led them to record five acclaimed albums over the years. The musicians are seasoned pros with twelve of the sixteen players being original members.

The music is lively and buoyant, including a slew of sturdy solos from various players. Members include pianist Steve Schmidt, trumpeter Hank Mautner, alto saxophonists Jim Sherrick and Mike Andres, baritone saxophonist Larry Dickson, tenor saxophonists Joe Gaudio and Herbie Aronoff, trombonists Paul Piller and Clarence Pond, bassist Michael Sharfe and drummer John Von Ohlen.

This is the kind of big band music that aficionados of the genre can appreciate and love to hear often which is why the Blue Wisp Big Band is still around and producing some of the finest orchestrations you'll hear anywhere.

Containing world-class horn players and bolstered by a superlative rhythm section, this group has established a reputation that extends far beyond Cincinnati and will hopefully keep them playing for years to come.
name: Blue Wisp Big Band

description:
Stan Kenton Alum John Von Ohlen kicks this band like no one else that iI can only describe as follows: ITS ALIVE! Don't try to analyze it, just feel it. Cammy award winner Steve Schmidt on piano and bassist MIke Sharfe drive this 17 piece band as well as anyone anywhere.

A legendary regional ensemble from Cincinnati, the Blue Wisp Big Band has, for the last thirty years, performed every Wednesday evening at the famed Blue Wisp Jazz Club in Cincinnati, owned and operated by Marjean Wisby until her passing in August 2006.

Having been around for a quarter of a century this big band knows how to play and does so with the same fire that has led them to record five acclaimed albums over the years. The musicians are seasoned pros with twelve of the sixteen players being original members.

The music is lively and buoyant, including a slew of sturdy solos from various players. Members include pianist Steve Schmidt, trumpeter Hank Mautner, alto saxophonists Jim Sherrick and Mike Andres, baritone saxophonist Larry Dickson, tenor saxophonists Joe Gaudio and Herbie Aronoff, trombonists Paul Piller and Clarence Pond, bassist Michael Sharfe and drummer John Von Ohlen.

This is the kind of big band music that aficionados of the genre can appreciate and love to hear often which is why the Blue Wisp Big Band is still around and producing some of the finest orchestrations you'll hear anywhere.

Containing world-class horn players and bolstered by a superlative rhythm section, this group has established a reputation that extends far beyond Cincinnati and will hopefully keep them playing for years to come.
name: Blue Wisp Big Band

description:
Stan Kenton Alum John Von Ohlen kicks this band like no one else that iI can only describe as follows: ITS ALIVE! Don't try to analyze it, just feel it. Cammy award winner Steve Schmidt on piano and bassist MIke Sharfe drive this 17 piece band as well as anyone anywhere.

A legendary regional ensemble from Cincinnati, the Blue Wisp Big Band has, for the last thirty years, performed every Wednesday evening at the famed Blue Wisp Jazz Club in Cincinnati, owned and operated by Marjean Wisby until her passing in August 2006.

Having been around for a quarter of a century this big band knows how to play and does so with the same fire that has led them to record five acclaimed albums over the years. The musicians are seasoned pros with twelve of the sixteen players being original members.

The music is lively and buoyant, including a slew of sturdy solos from various players. Members include pianist Steve Schmidt, trumpeter Hank Mautner, alto saxophonists Jim Sherrick and Mike Andres, baritone saxophonist Larry Dickson, tenor saxophonists Joe Gaudio and Herbie Aronoff, trombonists Paul Piller and Clarence Pond, bassist Michael Sharfe and drummer John Von Ohlen.

This is the kind of big band music that aficionados of the genre can appreciate and love to hear often which is why the Blue Wisp Big Band is still around and producing some of the finest orchestrations you'll hear anywhere.

Containing world-class horn players and bolstered by a superlative rhythm section, this group has established a reputation that extends far beyond Cincinnati and will hopefully keep them playing for years to come.
name: Blue Wisp Big Band

description:
Stan Kenton Alum John Von Ohlen kicks this band like no one else that iI can only describe as follows: ITS ALIVE! Don't try to analyze it, just feel it. Cammy award winner Steve Schmidt on piano and bassist MIke Sharfe drive this 17 piece band as well as anyone anywhere.

A legendary regional ensemble from Cincinnati, the Blue Wisp Big Band has, for the last thirty years, performed every Wednesday evening at the famed Blue Wisp Jazz Club in Cincinnati, owned and operated by Marjean Wisby until her passing in August 2006.

Having been around for a quarter of a century this big band knows how to play and does so with the same fire that has led them to record five acclaimed albums over the years. The musicians are seasoned pros with twelve of the sixteen players being original members.

The music is lively and buoyant, including a slew of sturdy solos from various players. Members include pianist Steve Schmidt, trumpeter Hank Mautner, alto saxophonists Jim Sherrick and Mike Andres, baritone saxophonist Larry Dickson, tenor saxophonists Joe Gaudio and Herbie Aronoff, trombonists Paul Piller and Clarence Pond, bassist Michael Sharfe and drummer John Von Ohlen.

This is the kind of big band music that aficionados of the genre can appreciate and love to hear often which is why the Blue Wisp Big Band is still around and producing some of the finest orchestrations you'll hear anywhere.

Containing world-class horn players and bolstered by a superlative rhythm section, this group has established a reputation that extends far beyond Cincinnati and will hopefully keep them playing for years to come.
name: Blue Wisp Big Band

Stan Kenton Alum John Von Ohlen kicks this band like no one else that iI can only describe as follows: ITS ALIVE! Don't try to analyze it, just feel it. Cammy award winner Steve Schmidt on piano and bassist MIke Sharfe drive this 17 piece band as well as anyone anywhere.

A legendary regional ensemble from Cincinnati, the Blue Wisp Big Band has, for the last thirty years, performed every Wednesday evening at the famed Blue Wisp Jazz Club in Cincinnati, owned and operated by Marjean Wisby until her passing in August 2006.

Having been around for a quarter of a century this big band knows how to play and does so with the same fire that has led them to record five acclaimed albums over the years. The musicians are seasoned pros with twelve of the sixteen players being original members.

The music is lively and buoyant, including a slew of sturdy solos from various players. Members include pianist Steve Schmidt, trumpeter Hank Mautner, alto saxophonists Jim Sherrick and Mike Andres, baritone saxophonist Larry Dickson, tenor saxophonists Joe Gaudio and Herbie Aronoff, trombonists Paul Piller and Clarence Pond, bassist Michael Sharfe and drummer John Von Ohlen.

This is the kind of big band music that aficionados of the genre can appreciate and love to hear often which is why the Blue Wisp Big Band is still around and producing some of the finest orchestrations you'll hear anywhere.

Containing world-class horn players and bolstered by a superlative rhythm section, this group has established a reputation that extends far beyond Cincinnati and will hopefully keep them playing for years to come.
name: Blue Wisp Big Band
